findings.title: Busy times are skipped for any slot inside a date override
findings.description: When a slot falls inside a date override, the function returns `true` at lines 133-135, before the `busy.every(...)` check at lines 153-180 runs. This early return applies to both fixed hosts (line 488) and loose hosts (line 513), since both spread `dateOverrides` and `busy` into `checkIfIsAvailable`. A calendar event or existing booking on a day with a date override therefore no longer blocks the slot. `getTimeSlots` in `packages/lib/slots.ts` does not consult busy times, so nothing else catches it. This is a double-booking regression. Neither the new test nor the existing "Check for Date overrides" test has any busy time on the override day.

findings.title: Any weekday with more than one working-hours row rejects every slot
findings.description: `workingHours.find(...)` returns truthy when any row for the slot's weekday does not contain the slot's start, and the caller reads that as "outside working hours". `getWorkingHours` in `packages/lib/availability.ts:76-100` emits one entry per availability row. A schedule with two rows on the same weekday, such as 09:00-12:00 and 13:00-17:00, therefore produces two entries. No slot is contained in both, so every slot on that weekday is rejected, including ones in the 09:00 block. Single-block schedules work, which is why the existing fixtures pass. The check should be "some row for this weekday contains the slot", using `some` and the positive condition.

findings.title: Multiple date-override rows on the same date reject the whole date
findings.description: `dateOverrides.find(...)` stops at the first override whose window does not contain the slot. The availability router stores each override range as its own row with `days: []` (`packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/availability.tsx:315-322`), and `getUserAvailability` returns one entry per row (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:215-224`). With two disjoint windows on one date, a slot inside the second window is rejected by the first window's check, and the reverse holds too. Every slot on that date is removed, even though `getSlots` in `packages/lib/slots.ts:245` generates slots from both windows.

findings.title: Override logic is duplicated across two modules and the two copies disagree
findings.description: `getSlots` already applies date overrides by replacing working hours (`packages/lib/slots.ts:210-246`). `checkIfIsAvailable` reimplements the same rule with different offset arithmetic (`slots.ts:107-108` versus `packages/lib/slots.ts:212-223`). The second copy is the source of the first and third FAILs, and it also uses `find` for side effects (`dateOverrideExist` is set inside the callback). The inline `{ start: Date; end: Date }[]` type duplicates the existing `TimeRange`/`DateOverride` type. Since `getSlots` already limits slots to override windows, the override block in `checkIfIsAvailable` could be removed, leaving the busy check in place.

findings.title: Date-override guard uses an identity comparison and server-local date formatting
findings.description: Line 114 compares two dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false, so the zero-length branch is dead. The intended check is `isSame`. Lines 109-111 format `dayjs(date.start).add(...)` in server-local mode but format `slotStartTime` in UTC (`slotStartTime = time.utc()`). On a server or developer machine that is not in UTC, the day comparison is off near midnight. Nothing in the test setup pins `TZ` (a grep of the repo found no `TZ` setting), so results can differ between machines.

findings.title: End-of-slot check compares the slot start, not the slot end
findings.description: `const end = slotStartTime.hour() * 60 + slotStartTime.minute();` is identical to the `start` line directly above it. The end of the slot is never compared against the working-hours end. `getTimeSlots` bounds may hide this today, but the check is wrong as written. It should use `slotEndTime`.

findings.title: Early-morning overrides can land on the wrong invitee day
findings.description: The offset direction is right for how `override.start` is built. `getUserAvailability` stores the organizer's wall-clock time with a UTC label (`packages/core/getUserAvailability.ts:218-223`), and `invitee - organizer` is the correct shift for that label. The problem is what happens after the shift. The day filter (lines 206-208) uses the unshifted label, but the minutes are reduced with `hour() * 60 + minute()` (lines 218-223), which drops the day change. When the shift crosses the invitee's midnight, the override lands on the wrong day. Example: organizer `Asia/Kolkata`, invitee UTC, override 00:30-02:00 on day D (organizer local). The correct result is D-1 19:00-20:30 UTC. The code keeps the override on day D and produces 19:00-20:30 there. The fix is to compute the shifted instant once and assign the day from it.

findings.title: New `timeZone` is typed optional but treated as required
findings.description: `TimeRange.timeZone` is optional, but `packages/lib/slots.ts:212-213` passes it straight to `.tz(...)` with no guard. In `checkIfIsAvailable`, a missing `organizerTimeZone` silently becomes UTC (`slots.ts:107`). The selected-slots branch passes `userSchedule?.timeZone` (`slots.ts:585`), which can be undefined. Correct results now depend on a field the type says may be absent. I could not confirm dayjs's fallback for `.tz(undefined)` because `node_modules` is not installed. A dedicated override type with a required `timeZone`, or an explicit error, would make the contract visible.

findings.title: New test duplicates an assertion and the fixture does not match real data
findings.description: The added block repeats the expected slots of the previous assertion under a different invitee timezone. It does not cover any of the failure modes above: busy time on an override day, two rows on one weekday, two overrides on one date, or a non-UTC organizer with overrides near midnight. The fixture `IstWorkHoursWithDateOverride` (lines 119-126) gives the override row `days: [0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6]`, but the router writes override rows with `days: []` (`availability.tsx:321`). With `days` set, `getWorkingHours` treats the override as a recurring 14:00-18:00 row every day, which is the FAIL 2 case. The test only asserts on the override day, so it does not show this. Fixing the fixture and adding cases for each FAIL above would cover them.

findings.title: Unrelated whitespace changes in the same diff
findings.description: The diff removes a blank line before `return true;` in `busy.every`, adds one after the loose-host block (around line 500), and removes one before the `isTimeWithinBounds` filter (around line 591). The changes are harmless, but they add noise to a functional change.

findings.title: Redundant Date-to-string round trip and repeated computation
findings.description: Lines 212-213 use `dayjs(override.start.toString())`, which round-trips the Date through a string and drops milliseconds. The adjacent lines use `dayjs(override.start)`. `dayjs(override.start).utc().add(offset, "minute")` is also computed four times for the start and end. Computing it once per bound would make the mapping easier to follow.
